placements.why: The document establishes that a rollback capability exists only when it has been rehearsed — a proof standard equating demonstration with possession. This calls for a Proof strata category to hold themes about capabilities validated through practice rather than assertion.
placements.title: From claimed capability to demonstrated capability
placements.frame: What here is being treated as real only because it has been demonstrated — and what would collapse if the demonstration were absent?

placements.title: a capability we have not rehearsed is a capability we do not actually have
placements.frame: Is operational readiness here being treated as real only when it has been demonstrated through rehearsal — not when it has been merely planned, claimed, or assumed?
placements.why: src-1 issues the aphoristic maxim that an unrehearsed rollback is no rollback at all, establishing the principle that capability requires demonstration. src-3 and src-4 ratify that principle into a recorded commitment — a monthly cadence with a named owner — converting the maxim into a recurring proof practice. The theme is that operational readiness is not a state you claim but a practice you demonstrate, and future envelopes feeding this leaf will keep testing where readiness is assumed versus where it is proven.
